v.why: A conv on edge 2 adds less when edge 0 already provides a conv feature at node 1, since deep chains saturate.
With a skip upstream, a conv on edge 2 adds a new learned transform on the path instead of a redundant one.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is zero and a conv on edge 2 acts on nothing, so it has no effect.
Edge 4 reads node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the conv is useless.
Edge 4 conv builds on a conv-processed node 1 and enlarges the receptive field for a deeper path.
Edge 5 reads node 2, which is partly dead when edge 1 is none, so the conv gains less.
Stacking convs along 0->2->3 gives a deeper hierarchical feature path that helps on harder datasets.
Pooling upstream already smooths features, so a 1x1 conv downstream adds little.
A direct skip into node 3 makes the longer conv path redundant.
The shortcut at node 3 reduces the marginal value of an additional conv path.
Without the direct edge, edge 4 conv is a main route into the output and matters more.
With edge 3 absent, edge 5 conv carries a larger share of the output signal.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv adds a whole path, a larger gain than replacing a skip.
Replacing a skip with a conv loses the clean gradient shortcut, so the gain is smaller than when replacing none.
Replacing a pool with a conv gains learnable capacity, more than replacing a conv-like op.
Adding a skip where nothing existed gives the largest gain by restoring a direct path.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip loses capacity, so the edit is harmful.
Replacing pooling on the input edge with a conv gains much more than replacing a skip.
Replacing a skip with a conv on edge 0 gives a smaller gain since the skip already preserves information.
When edge 0 pools, edge 1 conv gains from its direct access to raw input, so the sibling's weakness raises its value, but the node 1 path is partly redundant.
Pooling smooths input, and a following conv can extract features from the smoothed map.
Sibling convs at node 3 compete and are partly redundant when summed.
With no sibling on edge 5, edge 4 is the only route from node 1 and the conv matters more.
Edge 5 conv overlaps with an existing conv on edge 4 at the fan-in sum.
Without edge 4, edge 5 is the main conv route into node 3 and adds more.
Node 2 fan-in from a conv on edge 1 makes an additional conv on edge 2 partly redundant.
With edge 1 absent, edge 2 is the only feed into node 2 and the conv is more valuable.
Edge 1 conv competes with an existing conv on edge 2 at the node 2 sum.
A second skip into node 3 duplicates the existing shortcut and adds nothing.
